lives.drunk_smith: Another, and put it on the slate.
Who moved the anvil? Somebody moved the anvil.
My hands are steady. It's the world that shakes.
Iron and ale, the two things a smith needs.
Don't look at me, I'm resting my eyes.
One more and I'll go home. One more.
The lad does the bellows better than me now. Don't tell him.
Hot iron, cold ale. In that order.

lives.drunk_smith.text: Hey, {player}! Buy a smith a drink?

lives.drunk_smith: Steward wants his coin. Steward can want.
I made the lord's gate hinges, you know. Before.

lives.drunk_smith.text: Snow on the roof and fire in the belly.
Too hot for the forge. Too hot for anything but beer.

lives.drunk_smith.sober: Water, if you please. Just water.

lives.drunk_smith.sober.text: {player}! Come by the forge, I've not forgotten.

lives.drunk_smith.sober: Up at dawn with a clear head. Strange feeling.
lives.drunk_smith.forge_lost: The lad keeps the forge well. Better than I did.
I watch the carts now. Somebody has to.
Sit by me, old friend. Nobody listens to us anyway.
lives.widow_at_well: He used to carry the bucket.
The well's deep today. Or I'm tired.
Forty years, and now the bed's too big.
Don't mind me. I talk to the well.
Good water, this. He always said so.
You remind me of him, a little. Around the eyes.
I bake for two still. Habit.

lives.widow_at_well.text: Cold water on a cold morning. He'd laugh at me.

lives.widow_at_well: The little ones splash me. I let them.
I'll sit a moment. Just a moment.

lives.widow_at_well.text: The fjord took mine. The sea takes and takes.
The river gives and the river takes.

lives.young_lovers: Have you seen... no. Never mind.
Lovely evening for a walk. Alone. Entirely alone.
If anyone asks, I was at the well.
The stile at dusk. Nothing. Forget I said it.
My father would kill me. Slowly.
Flowers? These? Found them. On the ground.
Some families just can't let a ditch be a ditch.

lives.young_lovers.text: The stars are out. Somewhere someone's looking at them too.

lives.young_lovers: Don't tell my mother you saw me here.
I'm not blushing. It's the sun.
What do you know about eloping? Asking for a friend.
lives.ambitious_apprentice: First one in, last one out.
Watch this joint. Tight as a drum.
Two seasons more? I could do it now.
The master's old. Good, but old.
One day they'll come from the next town for my work.
Sleep is for journeymen. Oh. I am one.
I've a drawing for my masterpiece. Want to see?
Faster isn't worse. Faster is faster.
The guild will drink to me. You'll see.
My hands know the work before my head does.
Don't touch that, it's still hot.
lives.old_soldier: Three days at the ford. Three days.
Stand up straight, boy, you're not a sack of turnips.
We had no banners. We had mud.
I remember when this was all fields. Before the fields.
The bolt took me here. Still aches in the rain.
Did I tell you about the ford?
Young ones think war is songs. It's waiting, and feet, and mud.

lives.old_soldier.text: Noon. Time for the bench and the story.

lives.old_soldier: The lord's men march like ducks.
Keep your shield high and your mouth shut. Best advice I ever had.
We held. That's all there is to say. Then I'll say it again.

lives.old_soldier.text: Snow at the ford, too, in the second winter.
Sand in everything. In the bread, in the wounds.

lives.old_soldier.drills: Again! Until you can do it asleep.
lives.gossip: I'm not one to talk, but.
Did you hear about the miller's wife?
I only repeat what I'm told. Faithfully.
Who's that with the baker's boy? Interesting.
Well I never. Well I NEVER.
Some people should close their shutters.
Not that it's any of my business.

lives.gossip.text: {player}! Come here, I've heard something about you.

lives.gossip: Mark my words, there'll be a wedding.
Three nights running, the same door. Make of that what you will.
I saw nothing. Nothing at all. But.
lives.miser_merchant: Prices are fair. Fair for me.
Shut the door, the heat's getting out.
Every bit has a name. Mine.
You want a discount? I want a castle.
Mind the step. If you break it, you pay for it.
lives.healer: Wrap it tight and keep it dry.
Willow bark for the ache. Not too much.
Wash your hands. Please. Everyone. Wash your hands.
Rest, water, and a bit of broth.
The fever comes with the damp.
Bring me yarrow if you see it.
That's not a scratch, that's a gash. Come here.

lives.healer.text: Up all night with the miller's boy.

lives.healer: Sit. Let me look at you.
Eat something green, for goodness' sake.
lives.runaway: One day I'll see the sea.
Nobody leaves here. Except me. Someday.
I could walk to the next town in a day. Two at most.
Everyone here is old. Even the young ones.
Take me with you? Joking. Mostly.

lives.runaway.text: The carts leave at dawn. I watch them go.

lives.runaway: I've got a bundle. Just in case.
My father says the world's the same everywhere. How would he know?
Stars look different elsewhere, I bet.
Some day you'll hear of me. You'll see.
lives.poacher: Rabbit? Found it. Dead. On the road.
The lord has more deer than sense.
What snares? I've never seen a snare.
The woods are free. Or should be.

lives.poacher.text: Out late? So am I. We didn't see each other.

lives.poacher: Venison's a rich man's meat. Shame.
The steward walks like a cow. You hear him a mile off.
If anyone asks, I was home.
lives.miller_in_debt: The wheel turns and the debt grows.
Flour on everything. Even my worries.
Bad year, they say. Every year's a bad year.

lives.miller_in_debt.text: Up before the cock to beat the debt.

lives.miller_in_debt: The stones need dressing. Everything needs something.
My father never owed a bit in his life.
Harvest, they say. Pay by harvest.
A good mill, this. For now.
Weigh it twice; I'll not be called a cheat on top of the rest.
Bring your grain. I need the toll.
lives.pious_pilgrim: The shrine is far, but the road is holy.
I pray for this town. It needs it.
My mother walked it. Now I will.

lives.pious_pilgrim.text: Dawn prayers are the best heard.

lives.pious_pilgrim: Light a candle and the dark gets smaller.
Have you been to the shrine? You should.
Bare feet keep a pilgrim humble.
lives.exile_come_home: Twelve years. Not a day less.
They look at me like I still owe them.
The old inn's the same. Same stain on the same table.

lives.exile_come_home.text: A cup to forget, and one to remember.

lives.exile_come_home: I came back for my mother. That's all.
Say what you like. I've heard worse on the road.
The road teaches a man things.
I'd work, if anyone would have me.
Old wrongs keep longer than old wine.
lives.courting: Look, you can see the whole valley.
They'll be wondering where we are.
Do you think it'll be like this always?

lives.courting.text: The sun's going down on us.

lives.courting.flower: For you. Picked it on the way.
I found this and thought of you.
Don't laugh. It's a flower. For you.
lives.courting.thanks: I'll press it in a book.
lives.feud.insult: Look who it is. Mind your purse.
Your house always did smell of pigs.
Walk on. Nobody wants you here.
Thief's blood runs in that family.
Your father owes mine an apology, and a ditch.
Keep to your side of the lane.
lives.feud.answer: Say that again, I dare you.
At least my house pays its debts.
You'll be sorry you said that.
We'll see who's laughing at harvest.
lives.grief: I brought flowers. You never liked flowers.
The garden's grown wild without you.
lives.masterpiece: To the guild! To the work!
lives.condolence: Thank you. It helps, a little.
Everyone says sorry. You seem to mean it.
lives.peace.yes: Maybe you're right. It's gone on long enough.
Fine. I'll shake their hand. Once.
lives.peace.no: You don't know what they did.
lives.overheard.fire: That's {player}. Fought the fire with the buckets, they say.
That one carried water when the roof was alight.
If it weren't for {player} the whole street would've gone up.
lives.overheard.murder: Don't look. That's {player}. Killed a man, they say.
Blood on those hands. Walk on.
Murderer. Right here in the street.
lives.overheard.assault: That's the one who struck the cooper.
Keep your distance from {player}. Quick with the fists.
lives.overheard.quest: That's {player}. Did right by the town, they did.
{player}'s the one who helped the reeve.
Good sort, that one. Gets things done.
lives.overheard.let_down: Promised the earth, that one, and brought nothing.
Don't ask {player} for help. Won't come.
lives.overheard.defender: Stood at the gate when the beasts came. Brave as a bull.
lives.overheard.gift: {player} brought a gift for the bride. Generous.
Gave the old woman a present, did {player}. Kind.
lives.overheard.rescue: {player} pulled the boy out, they say.
That's who saved the miller's lad.
lives.overheard.donor: {player} paid for the new well. Can you believe it?
Open-handed, that one. Put coin in the works.
lives.overheard.fugitive: That's the one who ran from the guards.
Broke out of the jail, {player} did.
lives.overheard.punished: Saw {player} in the pillory. Paid for it, at least.
Did their time, that one. Fair's fair.
lives.overheard.round: {player} bought the house a round the other night!
Generous with the ale, that one.
lives.overheard.pious: {player} comes to mass. Good to see.
Sits at the back at service. Pious, for a stranger.
lives.overheard.trouble: That's who's been trampling the gardens.
lives.overheard.poacher: {player} had a deer of the lord's, they say.
lives.overheard.neighbour: {player} bought the house on the lane. A neighbour now.
lives.overheard.kindness: {player} helped one of ours when nobody else would.
{player} has a kind heart, they say.
lives.overheard.good: That one's done right by us.
lives.overheard.bad: Nothing good said of {player} in this town.
lives.overheard.answer.good: Good. We need more like that.
Buy them a drink if you see them.
